extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing or processing Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing, formatting, timing, and examiner handling of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, including e-IDS via EFS and procedures when the issue fee has been paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Information disclosure statements filed after the issue fee has been paid will not be considered by the Office but will be placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application may be withdrawn from issue (so the IDS can be considered) by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c)(2) with a RCE, or 1.313(c)(3) with a CPA or a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Petitions need not be accompanied by the IDS if the IDS is impracticable to fax, but should indicate that an IDS will be filed. The Office cannot ensure petition action prior to grant; applicants are encouraged to call Office of Petitions and to fax or hand-carry petitions. Alternatively, an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable over the information (for 1.313(c)(1)) may be filed to withdraw the application from issue; a mere statement of a 'serious question' is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) — two permitted statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) must state either (1) each item was first cited in a foreign patent office communication in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the statement, or (2) no item was so cited and, after reasonable inquiry, none was known to any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement may be in plain form (not necessarily oath/declaration). If some items meet (1) and others meet (2), two lists/statements may be included. The date on the foreign communication (mailing date if two dates present) begins the three-month period. A copy of the foreign search report alone is not sufficient to satisfy (1) because it may not show that the information was 'first cited' within three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and effect of 'counterpart foreign patent application'
rubrics_metrics.description: A counterpart foreign patent application exists where a priority claim is made in either application to the other, or the U.S. and foreign disclosures are substantively identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications from foreign offices that list family members (including U.S. patents or English-language patents) may be treated as the foreign office citing the U.S./English patent for purposes of 1.97(e)(1) if 1.97 and 1.98 are complied with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable inquiry requirement for 1.97(e)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A signer making the 1.97(e)(2) statement must, after making reasonable inquiry, believe that no item was known to any individual designated in 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner may rely on statements by a foreign client but must make reasonable inquiry if facts are unclear. If an inventor of the U.S. application is a named inventor of an item listed in the IDS, the 1.97(e)(2) statement cannot be made for that item. The statement may be based on present, good-faith knowledge without searching files; statements on information and belief are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules and filing date effect for statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement under 1.97(e) is considered filed on the date it is received by the Office, or on an earlier mailing/transmission date if accompanied by a proper certificate of mailing, facsimile transmission certificate under 37 CFR 1.8, or Express Mail compliance under 37 CFR 1.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office uses these dates to determine compliance with the 3-month timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time for filing IDS under 37 CFR 1.136
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are not permitted for filing an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with 1.98 but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance (see form paragraph 6.51), but no extensions under 1.136(a)/(b) are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review for compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners will review IDS submissions for compliance with timing and content requirements in 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 and will notify applicants of compliance or noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complying IDSs will be considered and handled like other prior art in Office search files; considered citations are initialed (or handled via electronic signature method) and returned to applicant with the next communication as acknowledgement and indication of which references were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncomplying IDS placement and non-consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS that does not comply with 1.97/1.98 (based on time of filing, missing fee, missing statement, or content deficiencies) will be placed in the application file but none of the information will be considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should mark such IDSs 'not considered' and notify applicant using form paragraphs 6.49–6.49.10 describing the deficiency. Applicant may file a corrected IDS, but the new submission date becomes the IDS date for timing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific content/form failures that render IDS items not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific noncompliance examples that cause items (or entire IDS) not to be considered include: lack of required 1.97(e) statement, lack of required fee (37 CFR 1.17(p)), listing references in the specification instead of a separate paper, missing copies of non-U.S. patents/NPLs/other info, non-compliant list format, no concise explanation for non-English references, and submission on unacceptable electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 6.49.01–6.49.10) to notify applicant. If only some items fail requirements, cross through the noncompliant citations and consider the rest. For IFW-stored U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications, copies need not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS list format requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS list must: (1) list all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted; (2) list U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications in a separate section from other documents; (3) include the application number on each page; (4) provide a blank space next to each document for examiner initials; and (5) have a heading clearly indicating the list is an information disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS list is non-compliant with these format elements the IDS may be placed in the file but not considered. Copying an initialed IDS listing from another application does not satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: IDS must include a legible copy of each cited foreign patent document, each non-patent literature publication (or the pertinent portion), and other information or the portion that caused it to be listed, unless the documents are U.S. patents/patent application publications stored in IFW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required copies leads to non-consideration of the affected items. Examiner note: do not use form paragraph for missing references that are U.S. patents/app publications stored in IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation for non-English references (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When non-English language information is cited in an IDS, a concise explanation of the relevance of each non-English reference, as presently understood by the individual in 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about its content, must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If absent, the IDS will be placed in the file but the information will not be considered. A translator need not be filed unless necessary; the examiner will consider non-English material to the extent understandable on its face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic medium acceptability and e-IDS via EFS rules
rubrics_metrics.description: IDSs may be electronically submitted via EFS/EFS-Web. e-IDS can include citations to U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature; for foreign docs, NPLs, or unpublished U.S. patent applications not in IFW, copies must be submitted in PDF via EFS-Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSs submitted on unacceptable electronic media (e.g., CDs, unsupported formats) will be placed in file but not considered; only tables, sequence listings, and program listings may be submitted on CDs. An e-IDS listing may contain up to 50 U.S. patents/pubs, 50 foreign docs, and 50 NPLs per listing; applicants may file multiple e-IDSs if limits exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner indication of consideration (initialing/electronic signature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must indicate which citations have been considered by initialing adjacent to considered citations on PTO/SB/08A and 08B (or equivalent) or by using an alternative electronic signature method stamping pages 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials and signing the final page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must also fill in name and date the information was considered on the form. For IFW processing, see IFW Manual. The copy returned to applicant with the next communication serves as acknowledgement and shows which references were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of documents submitted as part of applicant's reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted and relied upon by applicant in reply to an Office action (e.g., affidavits, patents, publications) need not comply with 1.97/1.98 to be considered by the examiner for the specific issue of patentability addressed in the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration is limited to the portion of the document relied upon as rebuttal evidence; the entire document may not be considered. Such documents need not be processed as items cited in an IDS, and special listing/marking on PTO forms is not required, but the record should reflect whether the evidence was considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when only some IDS requirements omitted inadvertently (one-month cure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDS complies with timing but part of the content requirements of 1.98(b) has been inadvertently omitted and the submission appears bona fide, applicant is given ONE MONTH to supply omissions or corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension of this one-month time limit may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b). This practice does not apply where there was deliberate omission or where timing requirements under 1.97 were not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking/cross-through of non-considered citations and printing on patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item in an IDS is not considered, a line should be drawn through the citation; considered citations will be initialed (or handled electronically). Citations considered and on PTO/SB/08A/08B (or equivalent) will be printed on the face of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For printing, lists must lend themselves to easy capture (each item on single line, double-spaced lines, uniform format). Citations printed from IDS will be distinguished from examiner-cited citations (examiner citations may be marked with an asterisk). If applicant does not provide classification info or incorrect data is lined through, the citation may be printed without classification. U.S. patent application numbers listed on PTO/SB/08A/08B and considered will be printed; applicants may list application numbers elsewhere to avoid publication on the patent.
